analysis:
This PR changes only a test file, provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Service/LaunchAgentLifecycleTests.swift. No production code is in the supplied evidence. The test change at line 466 flips the expectation for kickstartIfLoaded when launchctl reports the service as missing. The new expectation is `!kicked`, so the adapter must not report success for a vanished service.

The new WatchdogLaunchAdapterTests (lines 496-670) run the real LaunchAgent.kickstartIfLoaded adapter against a scripted launchctl. They check that recovery does not commit a KV-backend crash-loop guard trip when the service vanished. They also check that a pre-existing guard file stays byte-identical, that no enable/bootstrap is issued, that the plist is unchanged, and that the success and permission-failure paths behave as expected.

The tests only constrain behavior and add no attack surface. The temp home is used via task-local seams and all launchctl operations are intercepted. The WATCHDOG_ADAPTER_WITNESS print outputs only test fixture data, with no secrets.

The related threat is T-043, where watchdog rollback authority is the same replaceable binary. The tests tighten watchdog recovery semantics and do not weaken T-043. T-041 was supplied but does not relate to this change.

The product-side changes to LaunchAgent.kickstartIfLoaded, WatchdogRecoveryService and KVBackendCrashLoopGuard are outside this batch. Their correctness is not verified here. The tests assume `.noLongerLoaded` and `.restartIssued` outcomes that integration should confirm exist in the production code. No security regressions were found in the test changes.
